newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian to be president of U.N. general assembly.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian to be president of U.N. general assembly.

text.p: A career diplomat was set on Tuesday to become the first Malaysian elected to the post of president of the United Nations General Assembly.
U.N. officials said Razali Ismail would be appointed at the opening of the 51st session of the assembly, which is to be attended by dozens of world leaders and foreign ministers.

Razali will be presiding over the forum at a difficult time -- the United States has vowed to block the re-election of U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali even though he has widespread support among U.N. member states for a second term from the end of this year.

A secretary-general is appointed by the 185-member General Assembly on the recommendation of the 15-nation Security Council. The United States is one of five permanent members of the council with veto power.
Razali, 57, has been Malaysia's ambassador to the United Nations since June 1988 and has steered a number of U.N. bodies through various difficult negotiations.
Razali joined the foreign ministry in 1962 and is concurrently ambassador to Cuba and High Commissioner to Barbados, Jamaica, Saint Lucia and Trinidad and Tobago.
